selection_process: S. No. Component Marks
1 Preliminary Examination (Objective Type) 100
2(a) Main Examination - Written Examination (Subjective and Descriptive) 600
2(b) Main Examination - Interview / Personality Test 50
Total Main Examination 650
Paper Subject Marks Duration
Paper-I General English 150 2½ Hours
Paper-II Criminal Major Laws 150 3 Hours
Paper-III Criminal Minor Laws 150 3 Hours
Paper-IV Miscellaneous Laws 150 3 Hours
Selection to the post of Assistant Public Prosecutor is made through a competitive examination conducted in three stages:

The Preliminary Examination is only a screening test to shortlist candidates for the Main Examination and its marks are not counted in the final merit list. It comprises one paper of 100 Objective Type (MCQ) questions carrying 100 marks
with a duration of 2 hours. Each correct answer carries 1 mark

and 25% of the marks secured for a correct answer is deducted for each wrong response (negative marking); unattempted questions carry zero marks. Candidates securing the Commission-decided qualifying marks will be admitted to the Main Examination
in a ratio of up to 10 times the number of vacancies per category.
The Main Written Examination consists of 4 papers of 150 marks each (600 marks total)
all Subjective and Descriptive Answer type:
Candidates securing qualifying marks in the Main Written Examination will be shortlisted in a ratio of 1:2 (subject to a minimum of 5
with reference to category-wise vacancies) for the Personality Test/Interview
which carries 50 marks. The final Merit List (Select List) is prepared based on the combined marks of the Written Examination and Interview (650 marks total). In case of a tie
the candidate with higher marks in the Written Examination is placed higher; if the tie persists
the older candidate (by date of birth) is placed higher.
how_to_apply: Candidates fulfilling the eligibility conditions can apply for OPSC Assistant Public Prosecutor Apply Online through the following steps:
Visit the official OPSC website at https://www.opsc.gov.in and carefully go through the detailed Advertisement No. 09 of 2026-27.
Register/log in and fill up the online Proforma Application, ensuring all information entered is accurate before submission.

Upload scanned copies of the required documents/certificates listed under Para-12 of the advertisement, along with a recent passport-size photograph (unsigned and unattested, within six months), full signature, and Left-Hand Thumb Impression (LTI).
Pay the applicable examination fee (Rs. 700/- for candidates other than SC/ST/PwD) through the online payment mode.
Submit the online Registration to receive a unique Permanent Public Service Account Number (PPSAN).

Take a printout of the finally submitted online Registration/Re-registration and Application form, sign the declaration, and retain it along with copies of certificates/documents for submission as and when asked, including at document verification.
Applications received through any mode other than the OPSC online portal will not be accepted and will be summarily rejected.
important_instructions: The venue of both the Preliminary and Main Examination will be Kataka (Cuttack); detailed venue information will be intimated in due course. Government servants (temporary or permanent) applying must inform their Head of Office in writing and furnish a "No Objection Certificate" during document verification; they are advised to obtain the NOC well in advance. SEBC certificates must be issued on or after 29.08.2023 to be considered valid; those issued earlier will not be accepted. Women candidates belonging to SC/ST/SEBC must submit caste certificates showing "daughter of ___"; certificates by virtue of marriage ("wife of ___") are not acceptable. OBC certificates will not be accepted in lieu of an SEBC certificate. Every candidate selected for appointment shall be examined by the Medical Board; failure to satisfy the medical requirement will result in non-appointment. Candidates found guilty of malpractice, seeking illegal support, or submitting forged/manipulated documents will be disqualified and may be debarred permanently or for a specified period from any OPSC recruitment; candidates adopting unfair means in the Written Examination will be permanently debarred. Applications that are incomplete in any respect, including non-uploading of required documents, are liable for rejection without any correspondence. Mere empanelment in the select list does not confer any right to appointment unless the Government is satisfied, after due enquiry, that the candidate is suitable in all respects. Submission of an NPS application is mandatory for all recommended candidates at the time of joining Government service. Any complaint regarding conduct of the examination must be sent to the Grievance Wing of the Commission by email ([email protected]) within 7 (seven) days of completion of the examination.

content_sections.heading: OPSC Assistant Public Prosecutor Vacancy 2026
content_sections.text: A total of 172 vacancies (58 reserved for women) have been notified for the post of Assistant Public Prosecutor, as furnished by the Home Department, Government of Odisha. Out of the total 172 vacancies, horizontal reservation is also provided for Ex-Servicemen, Sports Persons and Persons with Disabilities (PwD), who will be adjusted against the categories to which they belong. The PwD reservation of 8 posts is further broken down by disability category as follows: Cat-I (Blind/Low Vision) – 1 post; Cat-II (Hard of Hearing) – 2 posts; Cat-III (Locomotor disabilities including One Leg, One Arm, Both Arms, Both Legs, Leprosy Cured, Dwarfism, Acid Attack Victims, etc.) – 2 posts; Cat-IV (Specific Learning Disability/Multiple Disability) – 3 posts. Persons with temporary disability are not eligible for this reservation.

content_sections.heading: OPSC Assistant Public Prosecutor Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: Candidates must meet the following OPSC Assistant Public Prosecutor Qualification requirements, assessed as per the notification dated 20.08.2026:

rows.details: Bachelor's Degree in Law from a recognised University
At least 2 (two) years of experience as a practising Advocate, supported by a certificate from the concerned District & Sessions Judge in the prescribed format at Annexure-B
Certificate of Enrolment under Bar Council of India / State Bar Council

Must be able to speak, read and write Odia, and must have passed either the Middle School standard language test in Odia conducted by the Board of Secondary Education, Odisha, or Matriculation (Class-X) with Odia as a subject
Must be a citizen of India

content_sections.heading: OPSC Assistant Public Prosecutor Age Limit
content_sections.text: The OPSC Assistant Public Prosecutor Age Limit is calculated as on 1st January 2026: Minimum age: 21 years Maximum age: 42 years Candidates must be born not earlier than 2nd January 1984 and not later than 1st January 2005 Age relaxation of 5 years for SEBC, SC, ST, Women and Ex-Servicemen candidates Age relaxation of 10 years for Persons with Disabilities whose permanent disability is 40% or more Cumulative age relaxation of 15 years for Persons with Disabilities belonging to SEBC/SC/ST categories A candidate covered under more than one relaxation category is eligible for only one benefit - whichever is most beneficial Date of birth entered in the High School Certificate (or equivalent) issued by the concerned Board/Council will only be accepted Candidates are advised to check whether they satisfy the prescribed age limit before applying. Use our online Age Calculator to calculate your exact age instantly.

content_sections.heading: OPSC Assistant Public Prosecutor Salary
content_sections.text: Selected candidates for the OPSC Assistant Public Prosecutor post will be placed in the pay scale of Rs. 44,900/- in Level 10 of the Pay Matrix under ORSP Rules, 2017, along with usual Dearness Allowance and other Allowances as may be sanctioned by the Government of Odisha from time to time. The notification states that all persons appointed under the Government of Odisha on or after 1st January 2005 are covered by the Contributory Pension Scheme under the Odisha Civil Services (Pension) Amendment Rules, 2005, and are not eligible for pension under the earlier Odisha Civil Service (Pension) Rules, 1992. faq.question: Q1. What is OPSC Assistant Public Prosecutor Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: It is a recruitment drive by the Odisha Public Service Commission, under Advertisement No. 09 of 2026-27, to fill 172 posts of Assistant Public Prosecutor in Group-B of the Odisha State Prosecution Service under the Home Department.

faq.question: Q2. How many vacancies are available in OPSC Assistant Public Prosecutor Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: A total of 172 vacancies (58 reserved for women) are notified, distributed as UR-86, SEBC-23, SC-27 and ST-36.

faq.question: Q3. What is the last date to apply for OPSC Assistant Public Prosecutor Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The online application window closes on 28 September 2026 at 5:00 P.M.

faq.question: Q4. What is the qualification required for OPSC Assistant Public Prosecutor Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Candidates must hold a Bachelor's Degree in Law from a recognised University and have at least 2 years of experience as a practising Advocate, along with knowledge of Odia.

faq.question: Q5. What is the age limit for OPSC Assistant Public Prosecutor Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Candidates must be between 21 and 42 years of age as on 1 January 2026, with age relaxation applicable for SEBC, SC, ST, Women, Ex-Servicemen and PwD candidates as per the notification.

faq.question: Q6. What is the application fee for OPSC Assistant Public Prosecutor Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Candidates other than SC, ST and PwD categories must pay Rs. 700/- online. SC, ST and PwD candidates are exempted from the fee.

faq.question: Q7. How can I apply online for OPSC Assistant Public Prosecutor Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Eligible candidates can apply only online through the official OPSC website (opsc.gov.in) between 28 August 2026 and 28 September 2026.

faq.question: Q8. What is the selection process for OPSC Assistant Public Prosecutor Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Selection is through three stages: a Preliminary Examination (100 marks, screening only), a Main Written Examination (600 marks across 4 papers), and an Interview/Personality Test (50 marks). Final merit is based on the Main Examination and Interview marks (650 total).

faq.question: Q9. What is the salary for OPSC Assistant Public Prosecutor?
faq.answer: Selected candidates will receive pay of Rs. 44,900/- in Level 10 of the Pay Matrix under ORSP Rules, 2017, plus usual Dearness and other Allowances.

faq.question: Q10. When will the OPSC Assistant Public Prosecutor Preliminary Examination be held?
faq.answer: The Preliminary Examination is tentatively scheduled for 1 November 2026 (Sunday); the detailed schedule and centre will be notified separately, and the exam will be held at Kataka (Cuttack).
